# Portfolio content inventory

> **Phase 4 supplement (November 26, 2026):** See [Phase 4 reconciliation](portfolio-phase-4.md) for the owner-approved decisions and focused accuracy changes. It supersedes conflicting historical holds; keep earlier records for provenance.

> **Phase 3B supplement (November 24, 2026):** See the [Phase 3B evidence register and outstanding decisions](portfolio-phase-3b.md) for verified project metrics, current publication metadata, research coverage, education holds and the historical PDF privacy audit. It supersedes earlier pending checks only where explicitly documented; remaining holds continue.

Phase 2 sources include the owner's approved brief, the site and PDFs at Phase 1 commit `551db40`, and read-only Git inspection of the three linked project repositories. Source locations below identify evidence without reproducing contact details from documents.

- **Owner-approved** means the owner supplied the public wording or underlying facts.
- **Repository-supported** means a file, byline, presentation, or Git record supports the scope shown. A résumé is a self-reported source. Git authorship supports file-level work and is insufficient for broader claims about project ownership or outcomes.
- **Hold** means evidence, attribution, or publication approval is pending. **Exclude** means the material stays out of the redesigned site and remains available in Git history.

## Résumé and profile decisions

- **Résumé.** Reserve `assets/docs/mercy-amankwah-resume.pdf` as the future general professional résumé. Hide its call to action until the owner provides and approves a public copy. The homepage currently links the master CV and the alternate biography points to an older CV. Neither belongs in the default slot, and an application-specific résumé is also unsuitable. Leave the four existing Mercy PDF paths as compatibility paths for planning purposes. Before public release, have the owner review their continued direct exposure and record any privacy-driven retirement explicitly. [Existing homepage link](../index.html#L145)
- **LinkedIn and GitHub.** Recommend LinkedIn as the primary professional contact link and GitHub as a secondary technical profile. The LinkedIn URL comes from the current site and still needs an owner click-through. The `mgamankwah` GitHub identity is consistent with the site, readable project repositories and the Alzheimer's team credit. Confirm the preferred contact channel. Add a public email only if the owner designates one.
- **Google Scholar.** The two candidates are `fmZ8W3gAAAAJ` in the hero and `-MZ1OlcAAAAJ` in the footer. HTTPS requests to both were blocked. Leave Scholar out of the redesigned navigation and footer until the owner or a follow-up check matches named author and affiliation using the 2022 QPIXL paper `10.1038/s41598-022-11024-y`, the 2024 quantum-parallel paper `10.1038/s41598-024-53720-x` and the 2024 Bayesian muscle recruitment paper `10.1016/j.chaos.2024.115082`. Prefer a clean profile URL without account-session parameters after verification. The third Scholar ID on the Bashir-branded pages is excluded. [Hero link](../index.html#L133) · [Footer link](../index.html#L339)
- **Other profiles.** ResearchGate, Kaggle and historical social links are optional. Confirm ownership, current URL and relevance before including them. Omit generic social placeholders.

Git read access worked for all three linked project repositories. The environment proxy blocked the live Pages site, both Scholar profiles, LinkedIn, and sampled publisher and institutional endpoints, including Crossref, arXiv, SIAM, CWRU and Berkeley Lab. Research claims marked repository-supported rely on the inspected source records, and the inventory leaves live link and attribution checks pending where applicable.
